content_html_sanitized:
Nonetheless, everything seemed set for the bill to be announced in Parliament, until the Justice Minister, Martin Cauchon, went to Washington to ask permission of his handlers in DEAland. Now the Canadian media are reporting that the bill will be introduced sometime before Parliament's summer break. Cauchon insisted he was not consulting but only informing Ashcroft what Ottawa had decided to do.
See
 Three Separate Canadian Stories May 13, 2003. You Connect The Dots. Steve Tuck's Hearings; Canadian Justice Minister Grovels Toward Gomorrah, DC That Is. And A Subtle Twist In The Party Line.

Perhaps because not all of the problems are in Washington.

Health Minister Ann McLellan is sort of John Walters in drag. CBC said that she sounded more like she was back in her old Justice portfolio said she sympathized with police who claim they don't have the resources to target growing operations.

To say that she sympathizes with police is an understatement. She really seems to view her job as Health Minister as protecting the narks against the sick and dying.
See
 Health Canada's Office of Cannabis Medical Access' Stakeholder Advisory Committee Includes Physicians for A Smoke Free Canada - Not The Compassion Societies. But It Will Let Them Talk For An Hour
and
 The Slow Motion Murder of Michael Patriquen. Canada Really Does Have A Death Penalty, But Only for Medical Cannabis Patients. Breaking Their Own Laws To Follow the Prohibitionist Party Line.
and
 Canadian Health Minister Seeks Asylum In DEAland; Says Making Her Think About Medical Cannabis Constitutes Torture. In DC They Don't Allow That Sort of Thing. Thinking, That Is.
and
 Great Canadian Editorial Calls for Legalization; Decries Justice Minister's Giving Narks Veto Over Changing Marijuana Laws.

In the last few days, she has really gone around the bend. McLellan said, " The United States has every right to be upset that we've got so many of these illegal grow ops in places like the interior of British Columbia. We have got to make sure we are providing the resources to shut them all down.

" Some of this stuff from B.C. is now ending up in the streets of Mexico City. That is simply unacceptable and that is where interdiction is important. "

First, anyone so detached from reality as to think that Canadian law enforcement is going to come close to providing the resources to shut them all down, has no business in public office. Just how is this going to happen when DEAland produces vastly more cannabis than does Canada despite vast resources and draconian penalties for growing?

Second, the idea that BC Bud is now ending up in the streets of Mexico City defies all logic. After all, why by-pass the DEAland market where they could get top dollar to go to a country that is the world's largest producer of cannabis, some of which is of outstanding quality.

MarijuanaNews archives can trace that little jewel back to her hometown police in 1998. Only then it was supposed to be Edmonton that was becoming a marijuana exporter as local drug growers ship their illegal products to British Columbia, the U.S. and even Mexico, local police are warning after their latest bust.
See
 Edmonton Police Actually Claim That Canadian Marijuana Is Being Exported To Mexico If You Believe That

McLellan's wins her seat in parliament by a very narrow margin, so Canadian cannabis laws are being set in a marginal riding in a conservative area. What a way to make national policy!

Now Canadian Press reports, Canada must be prepared for a potential increase in marijuana use - at least in the short run - if simple possession of pot is decriminalized, says Health Minister Anne McLellan.

Reports from U.S. states that have dropped criminal sanctions indicate there's a spike in use immediately after the law is changed, McLellansaid Wednesday as she left a Liberal caucus meeting. She said use levels eventually drop back to normal but it's important to be prepared all the same.

Of course, the data shows nothing of the sort. Consider these two items from the NORML website:

 " In sum, there is little evidence that decriminalization of marijuana use necessarily leads to a substantial increase in marijuana use. " - National Academy of Sciences, Institute of Medicine (IOM). 1999. Marijuana and Medicine: Assessing the Science Base. National Academy Press: Washington, D.C., 102.

" The Law Revision Commission has examined laws from other states that have reduced penalties for small amounts of marijuana and the impact of those laws in those states. ... Studies of [those] states found (1) expenses for arrest and prosecution of marijuana possession offenses were significantly reduced, (2) any increase in the use of marijuana in those states was less than increased use in those states that did not decrease their penalties and the largest proportionate increase occurred in those states with the most severe penalties, and (3) reducing the penalties for marijuana has virtually no effect on either choice or frequency of the use of alcohol or illegal 'harder' drugs such as cocaine. "
" Certainly one has to be ready to deal with that spike, " she said. " It can lead to addiction, it can lead to all sorts of situations within local communities.
See
 The Gateway Theory Won't Die Because It Tells Prohibitionists Something They Want to Believe, But The Truth Tells Them Something They Refuse to Hear.

You need to be ready with information, with education, and with treatment. "
See
 Walters Tells a New Lie. Oh Happy Day! People Need Treatment If They Are Sent to Treatment, By Definition. And How Do They Treat Marijuana Addicts? We Couldn't Make This Up, But They Did.

Now when one considers that the Health Minister of Canada is so ignorant of the literature on the subject it would indeed seem that it is we who need to be ready with information, with education, and with treatment. "
See
 The Need For Drug Prohibition Education.Analysis By Richard Cowan.
How Can Parents Tell Their Children The Truth In A Sea Of Lies About Marijuana?

Then there is the problem with organized quackery. The Canadian Medical Association has said in the past that it favors decriminalization.
For the punch line see
Canadian Medical Association Passes Resolution Urging Possession Of Marijuana
Not Be Punishable By A Jail Term

However, it now says, While the CMA agrees that the consequences of a criminal conviction for possession of a small amount of marijuana for personal use are disproportionate to the potential harm, it is critical that any change to the legal status of marijuana neither encourage nor promote the normalization of its use.

" To proceed with decriminalization outside a comprehensive national drug strategy would be irresponsible, " said CMA President, Dr. Dana Hanson. " We are concerned the government will only introduce half-measures and not the comprehensive national drug strategy that is truly needed to effectively address illicit drug use and addiction. "

Key elements of a comprehensive national drug strategy would include: prevention and education programs to deter usage and the stigma associated with addiction; treatment and rehabilitation program for those who are addicted; increased research on the cause, effects, treatment options and the long-term health effects of addiction; and, a rigorously monitored evaluation system to ensure that progress is being made to combat drug use and addiction.
For the full text see http://www.cannabisnews.com/news/thread16289.shtml

In other words, while the consequences of a criminal conviction for possession of a small amount of marijuana for personal use are disproportionate to the potential harm, Canada must keep inflicting that disproportionate harm until there is a prohibitionist propaganda campaign in place to justify maintaining the black market. This idiotic advice comes from a group that has been unable to educate its members about the medical uses of cannabis.
See
 Live Free or Die In Pain. The Ignorance and Arrogance of the Quacks Who Deny Pain Relief to the Sick and Dying.
and links

The fact is that decriminalization is a half measure that no longer makes any sense. Even some prohibitionists say that they would prefer legalization, because what is being proposed will just leave the production in the black markets.

All of this nonsense simply proves that Canada desperately needs a national debate on cannabis prohibition.
See
Canadian Justice Minister Calls for National Debate On Cannabis Policies And Begins It By Debating Himself. Phony Decrim Bill May Be Used As Cover To Increase Penalties for Growing.
